content.title: Don't Miss This Study: Genesis 18-23
content.summary: Dave Butler and Grace Freeman continue Abraham's story through Genesis 18-23, exploring themes of radical hospitality and divine provision. The episode reveals a God who shows up, pursues, and provides throughout these pivotal chapters. Additional resources including videos, prayer posters, and study materials for various age groups are available on the Don't Miss This website.

content.title: Genesis 18-23 with Dr. Carli Anderson (Part 1 & 2)
content.summary: Dr. Carli Anderson joins hosts Hank Smith and John Bytheway to explore Genesis 18-23 through Hebrew textual analysis, examining the stories of Abraham, Sarah, and Hagar. The two-part episode reveals the legal and linguistic depth of these foundational narratives, reframing Sarah, Hagar, and Abraham as parallel figures of faith whose choices, trials, and covenant roles demonstrate deeper layers of wisdom, agency, and trust in God's promises.
content.hosts_or_guests: Hank Smith, John Bytheway, Dr. Carli Anderson

content.title: Episode 360 - Genesis 18-23 (Come Follow Me 2026)
content.summary: Episode 360 covers Genesis 18-23 for the Come Follow Me lesson of February 23-March 1, 2026. The episode explores temple imagery through covenant, a sacred well, and a tree at Beer-sheba, discusses the burial of Sarah, and examines Abraham's sacrifice of Isaac on Mount Moriah as a type of Jesus Christ.

note: Behind Living Scriptures+ paywall. 2022 OT episode exists in archive.

content.title: Would God Really Ask Abraham to Sacrifice His Covenant Son?—Come Follow Me: Genesis 18-23
content.summary: This week's Come Follow Me lesson covers Genesis chapters 18-23, focusing on Abraham and Sarah with direct application to modern readers. The content explores the question of whether God would truly ask Abraham to sacrifice his covenant son. Available as both an article and podcast episode featuring presentations by Scot and Maurine Proctor.

note: Likely publishes 5x/week for this content block. Content lives primarily in podcast apps (not indexable via web search). Host: Cali Black.
Appears inactive since March 2024. 2022 OT archive episode exists but no 2026 content found.

content.title: Genesis 18-23 — Come, Follow Me Teaching Ideas
content.summary: Benjamin Wilcox (BA/MA English Literature) offers practical teaching ideas, discussion prompts, and downloadable lesson materials for Genesis 18-23. Especially useful for Gospel Doctrine teachers — includes slides, handouts, and classroom activities.

content.title: 2026 All Lessons — Come Follow Me Daily
content.summary: Aggregator site listing all available CFM content from dozens of creators, organized by week. A useful hub for finding additional creators beyond EVM's catalog, and a good cross-reference for URL verification.

content.title: Is Any Thing Too Hard for the Lord? Come, Follow Me Study Guide
content.summary: LDS Daily's weekly study guide for Genesis 18-23 provides historical context, reflection questions, curated leader quotes, and links to other creators' episodes for the week. Functions as both a study resource and an aggregator for the CFM community.

source_name: Scripture Central — Finding Christ in the OT

content.title: Is Anything too Hard for the Lord? (Class 9)
content.summary: John Hilton III traces Christological patterns across Genesis 18-23, showing how each narrative — the divine visitors, the intercession for Sodom, the birth of Isaac, the binding on Moriah — prefigures the Atonement. Companion resources available at johnhiltoniii.com/findingchrist.

content.title: Genesis 18-23 | Handmaidens, Harems and Heroines
content.summary: Lynne Hilton Wilson reframes Sarah and Hagar as vital covenant participants rather than background figures. Using feminist-scholarly LDS analysis and deep cultural and linguistic context, she recovers the full agency and spiritual significance of both women in these foundational narratives.

content.title: Genesis 18-23: Abraham & Isaac
content.summary: Jared Halverson delivers a 4-hour verse-by-verse study of Genesis 18-23, covering the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Hagar's wilderness encounter, and the Abrahamic test in forensic detail. The longest-form CFM content available — closest in format to EVM's own Deep Dive.

source_name: Church News — What Have Leaders Said

content.title: What Have Church Leaders Said About Genesis 18-23?
content.summary: The Church News compiles fully attributed prophetic quotes for this week's CFM lesson — President Faust on the seed of Abraham, Elder Holland on Lot's wife, President Hinckley on God's protective care. Each quote includes speaker, talk title, and date. A key source for quote verification.

content.title: Genesis 18-23 (Come Follow Up)
content.summary: James Goldberg and Deidre Green join host Ben Lomu on the BYUtv panel for a nuanced discussion of Genesis 18-23, exploring the theology of intercession, the complex ethics of Sodom and Gomorrah, and the covenant dimensions of the Abrahamic test. (2022 episode re-aired for 2026 season.)
content.hosts_or_guests: Ben Lomu, James Goldberg, Deidre Green

content.title: Come Follow Me March 2026 Old Testament Lesson Activities (Weeks 9-13)
content.summary: Printable lesson activities, song visuals, and age-specific resources (ages 1-16) for Genesis 18-23. Covers Primary and family home evening formats — ideal for parents and Primary teachers wanting hands-on materials for this week's stories.

content.title: Genesis 18-23: Switchpoints / A Well in the Wilderness / Withholding Nothing
content.summary: Emily Freeman and David Butler's original 2022 take on Genesis 18-23 centers on three powerful images: switchpoints (moments of divine re-routing), a well in the wilderness (Hagar's encounter with 'the God who sees'), and withholding nothing (Abraham's ultimate test). A different lens from the 2026 episode.
